items.q: The first pathogenic step of DKD is:
opts: Afferent arterial vasodilation + efferent arterial vasoconstriction
Efferent arteriolar vasodilation alone, without afferent change
Glomerular ischemia with low filtration pressure
Tubular atrophy with secondary interstitial scarring
items.exp: Pathogenesis: afferent arterial vasodilation + efferent arterial vasoconstriction → glomerular hyperfiltration → intraglomerular hypertension. (Book p815)

items.q: Match the following factor to the arteriolar tone it drives — 1) NO bioavailability  2) Prostaglandins  3) Angiotensin II  4) Thromboxane A2 … A) Net ↓ afferent arteriolar resistance  B) Net ↑ efferent arteriolar resistance
items.exp: Net ↓ afferent resistance: NO bioavailability, prostaglandins, kallikrein-kinins, atrial natriuretic factor, angiotensin (↓). Net ↑ efferent resistance: angiotensin II, thromboxane A2, endothelin-1 (ETA receptor). (Book p815)

items.q: All but one are listed as causing a net reduction of afferent arteriolar resistance. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Afferent list: NO bioavailability, prostaglandins, kallikrein-kinins, atrial natriuretic factor, angiotensin (↓); thromboxane A2 is on the efferent list. (Book p815)

items.q: The factors causing a net increase of efferent arteriolar resistance are:
items.exp: Efferent list: angiotensin II, thromboxane A2, endothelin-1 (ETA receptor). (Book p815)

items.q: Endothelin-1 drives efferent arteriolar resistance through the ETA receptor.
opts: False — it acts via the ETB receptor
False — it acts on the macula densa
True, but only in type 1 DM
items.exp: Endothelin-1 (ETA receptor) is on the efferent list. (Book p815)

items.q: The net result of the tone changes in DKD is:
In normal physiology (panel A), the afferent tone is:
opts: Appropriate, with normal TGF and normal GFR
Fixed, with no TGF at all
items.exp: A — normal physiology: normal TGF, normal GFR, appropriate afferent arterial tone. (Book p815)

items.q: In early diabetic nephropathy (panel B), the defect is:
opts: Afferent vasodilation + increased Na/glucose reabsorption → ↓ Na delivery to macula densa
Efferent dilation with increased Na delivery to the macula densa
Macula densa hyperplasia with fixed TGF
items.exp: B — hyperfiltration in early stages: afferent arterial vasodilation, increased Na/glucose reabsorption, decreased Na⁺ delivery to macula densa → impaired TGF, elevated GFR. (Book p815)

items.q: SGLT2 inhibition (panel C) restores the TGF because it:
opts: Raises Na⁺ delivery to the macula densa via reduced proximal reabsorption
Lowers Na⁺ delivery to the macula densa via enhanced reabsorption
Blocks the macula densa sensing entirely
items.exp: C — SGLT-2 inhibition in proximal tubule → increased Na⁺ delivery to macula densa → afferent arterial constriction → normalization of GFR; glucosuria. (Book p815)

items.q: Fill up: SGLT2 inhibitors raise Na⁺ entry to the ______, constricting the afferent arteriole.
items.exp: ↑ Na⁺ entry to macula densa → afferent arteriole constriction → ↓ GFR → ↓ hyperfiltration injury. (Book p815)

items.q: SGLT2 inhibitors are the 1st line management for hyperfiltration injury.
opts: False — they are for hypertension only
True, but only in type 1 DM

items.q: A diabetic with early nephropathy has an elevated GFR from afferent vasodilation. The mechanism by which an SGLT2 inhibitor normalizes the GFR is:
opts: Increased Na⁺ delivery to the macula densa → afferent constriction
Direct dilation of the efferent arteriole, with no TGF change
Suppression of renin release alone, without TGF
Osmotic diuresis from the induced glucosuria
items.exp: SGLT-2 inhibition → increased Na⁺ delivery to macula densa → afferent arteriole constriction → normalization of GFR. (Book p815)

items.q: All but one are labelled structures in the hyperfiltration diagram. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Diagram labels: afferent arteriole, efferent arteriole, macula densa, juxtaglomerular cells, podocyte, proximal tubule. (Book p815)
